CLM-0004 [verified]: The contract surface is frozen at exactly five types — TaskContract, Brief, Verdict, Outcome, Manifest — and references to any contract outside the five are rejected.

CLM-0007 [verified]: claims:check fails on dangling evidence — a test ref naming a nonexistent test, a CI ref naming a nonexistent job, a doc ref with a missing anchor, or an eval ref pointing at a missing artifact each exit the gate red.

CLM-0009 [verified]: Every audit event is hash-chained: a chain of appended events verifies end-to-end with its exact length.
CLM-0010 [verified]: Every audit envelope carries the contracts surface version it was written under.

CLM-0012 [verified]: Truncating, reordering, or deleting audit log entries fails verification.
CLM-0013 [verified]: Tamper evidence is property-tested: across seeded random chains, every single-byte mutation of the audit log file fails verification.

CLM-0015 [verified]: The manifest registry rejects invalid manifests at registration and is the single source of capability truth for lookup.

sections.name: plan
sections.content:
The plan is grounded: `skills/README.md` is currently five lines and already gestures at the distill path, and `skills/proposed/run-quality-gate-via-kernel/` exists as a live example of a suggest-tier proposal. Here is the PM decomposition.

## Implementation plan — append "Ratification path (P3)" to skills/README.md

**Scope assessment.** This is a single-file documentation task with no code, no new claims, and no contract changes. Both capability statements it documents are already verified (CLM-0049, CLM-0050), so the work is purely descriptive and the honest decomposition is one child task. Splitting further would burn budget on coordination for a section of prose.

**Child 1 of 1 — Documenter: write the section.**

*Goal.* Append a `## Ratification path (P3)` section to `skills/README.md`, leaving the existing five lines untouched. The section must state, in this order: (1) `distill` proposes a `SKILL.md` from an episodic trace and writes it to `skills/proposed/<name>/`, entering the authority ladder at **suggest** tier `[CLM-0049]`; (2) a proposed skill goes live only when a human moves `skills/proposed/<name>/` to `skills/<name>/` through a reviewed PR — that merge **is** the ratification, and skills enter the procedural library through no other path `[CLM-0050]`. It may cite the live example `skills/proposed/run-quality-gate-via-kernel/` as the current state of the queue. Every capability sentence carries its claim tag per the charter; no sentence may claim behavior beyond what CLM-0049/0050 attest.

*Files owned.* `skills/README.md` only. Any discovery outside this file (e.g., stale wording elsewhere) is reported back, not acted on.

*Evidence requirements.* No new claim entries — both claims exist and are verified. Evidence at integration: a diff whose only touched file is `skills/README.md`; the two claim tags present and resolving under `claims:check`; `governance:check` green (charter/doc consistency); lint green (LOC limits irrelevant here but the gate still runs).

*Definition of done.* Section appended; existing intro text unmodified; both claim tags present; `pnpm lint`, `pnpm claims:check`, and `pnpm governance:check` all green; quality gate emits a passing Verdict that appends to the audit chain. Done is the Verdict, not the diff.

*Budget slice.* The child receives **70%** of the parent budget on every metered dimension — tokens, usd, wall-clock duration — with authorityCeiling **suggest** (documentation proposal; the merge authority stays human). The parent PM retains the remaining **30%** as reserve for gate re-runs across the bounded vote-iterate cycle (K ≤ 3 per CLM-0043) and for integration verification. Sums check trivially: 70% + 30% = 100% on each dimension, within the parent on all three.

**Integration.** PM verifies the single-file constraint on the returned diff, runs the full gate suite, and routes the Verdict back through the loop. If the gate fails twice on wording (claim-tag or governance findings), iterate within K; on K exhaustion, escalate to the human rather than loosening the gate.

One open ambiguity, resolved narrow: the existing README line "enter only through the `distill` ratification path" slightly predates the new section and could be folded into it, but the brief says append and modify only — so the child appends and leaves that line alone; the PM notes the minor redundancy in the session report.

**Scope assessment.** This is a single-file documentation task with no code, no new claims, and no contract changes. Both capability statements it documents are already verified (CLM-0049, CLM-0050), so the work is purely descriptive and the honest decomposition is one child task. Splitting further would burn budget on coordination for a section of prose.

**Child 1 of 1 — Documenter: write the section.**

*Goal.* Append a `## Ratification path (P3)` section to `skills/README.md`, leaving the existing five lines untouched. The section must state, in this order: (1) `distill` proposes a `SKILL.md` from an episodic trace and writes it to `skills/proposed/<name>/`, entering the authority ladder at **suggest** tier `[CLM-0049]`; (2) a proposed skill goes live only when a human moves `skills/proposed/<name>/` to `skills/<name>/` through a reviewed PR — that merge **is** the ratification, and skills enter the procedural library through no other path `[CLM-0050]`. It may cite the live example `skills/proposed/run-quality-gate-via-kernel/` as the current state of the queue. Every capability sentence carries its claim tag per the charter; no sentence may claim behavior beyond what CLM-0049/0050 attest.

*Files owned.* `skills/README.md` only. Any discovery outside this file (e.g., stale wording elsewhere) is reported back, not acted on.

*Evidence requirements.* No new claim entries — both claims exist and are verified. *Budget slice.* The child receives **70%** of the parent budget on every metered dimension — tokens, usd, wall-clock duration — with authorityCeiling **suggest** (documentation proposal; the merge authority stays human). The parent PM retains the remaining **30%** as reserve for gate re-runs across the bounded vote-iterate cycle (K ≤ 3 per CLM-0043) and for integration verification. Sums check trivially: 70% + 30% = 100% on each dimension, within the parent on all three.

**Integration.** PM verifies the single-file constraint on the returned diff, runs the full gate suite, and routes the Verdict back through the loop. If the gate fails twice on wording (claim-tag or governance findings), iterate within K; on K exhaustion, escalate to the human rather than loosening the gate.

Claim tags on every capability sentence match the [CLM-xxxx] convention enforced by governance:check. Testability and workflow integration are strong: done is defined as gates green (lint, claims:check, governance:check) plus a quality-gate Verdict appended to the audit chain, all of which are existing automated pipelines — progress is verifiable at the single integration point, which is appropriate for a one-step task. sections.content:
The plan is grounded: `skills/README.md` is currently five lines and already gestures at the distill path, and `skills/proposed/run-quality-gate-via-kernel/` exists as a live example of a suggest-tier proposal. Here is the PM decomposition.

## Implementation plan — append "Ratification path (P3)" to skills/README.md

**Scope assessment.** This is a single-file documentation task with no code, no new claims, and no contract changes. Both capability statements it documents are already verified (CLM-0049, CLM-0050), so the work is purely descriptive and the honest decomposition is one child task. Splitting further would burn budget on coordination for a section of prose.

**Child 1 of 1 — Documenter: write the section.**

*Goal.* Append a `## Ratification path (P3)` section to `skills/README.md`, leaving the existing five lines untouched. The section must state, in this order: (1) `distill` proposes a `SKILL.md` from an episodic trace and writes it to `skills/proposed/<name>/`, entering the authority ladder at **suggest** tier `[CLM-0049]`; (2) a proposed skill goes live only when a human moves `skills/proposed/<name>/` to `skills/<name>/` through a reviewed PR — that merge **is** the ratification, and skills enter the procedural library through no other path `[CLM-0050]`. It may cite the live example `skills/proposed/run-quality-gate-via-kernel/` as the current state of the queue. Every capability sentence carries its claim tag per the charter; no sentence may claim behavior beyond what CLM-0049/0050 attest.

*Files owned.* `skills/README.md` only. Any discovery outside this file (e.g., stale wording elsewhere) is reported back, not acted on.

*Evidence requirements.* No new claim entries — both claims exist and are verified. Evidence at integration: a diff whose only touched file is `skills/README.md`; the two claim tags present and resolving under `claims:check`; `governance:check` green (charter/doc consistency); lint green (LOC limits irrelevant here but the gate still runs).

*Definition of done.* Section appended; existing intro text unmodified; both claim tags present; `pnpm lint`, `pnpm claims:check`, and `pnpm governance:check` all green; quality gate emits a passing Verdict that appends to the audit chain. Done is the Verdict, not the diff.

*Budget slice.* The child receives **70%** of the parent budget on every metered dimension — tokens, usd, wall-clock duration — with authorityCeiling **suggest** (documentation proposal; the merge authority stays human). The parent PM retains the remaining **30%** as reserve for gate re-runs across the bounded vote-iterate cycle (K ≤ 3 per CLM-0043) and for integration verification. Sums check trivially: 70% + 30% = 100% on each dimension, within the parent on all three.

**Integration.** PM verifies the single-file constraint on the returned diff, runs the full gate suite, and routes the Verdict back through the loop. If the gate fails twice on wording (claim-tag or governance findings), iterate within K; on K exhaustion, escalate to the human rather than loosening the gate.

One open ambiguity, resolved narrow: the existing README line "enter only through the `distill` ratification path" slightly predates the new section and could be folded into it, but the brief says append and modify only — so the child appends and leaves that line alone; the PM notes the minor redundancy in the session report.

sections.content:
CLM-0001 [verified]: Kernloop's five contracts are zod-validated: malformed messages — missing fields, unknown enum values, wrong types, negative budgets — are rejected at parse time.
CLM-0002 [verified]: The authority ladder is a closed four-tier enum — observe, suggest, advisory, enforce — and any other tier value is rejected at parse time.
CLM-0003 [verified]: All five contracts survive JSON round-trip serialization: parsing the stringified form of a valid contract yields a value equal to the original.
CLM-0004 [verified]: The contract surface is frozen at exactly five types — TaskContract, Brief, Verdict, Outcome, Manifest — and references to any contract outside the five are rejected.
CLM-0005 [verified]: Manifests carry governance as data: authority tier, maturity, optional promotion threshold, and claim references are schema-enforced, with unknown tiers and malformed claim ids rejected at parse time.
CLM-0006 [verified]: All five contracts reject unknown top-level keys, so field drift fails at parse time instead of passing silently across the bus.
CLM-0007 [verified]: claims:check fails on dangling evidence — a test ref naming a nonexistent test, a CI ref naming a nonexistent job, a doc ref with a missing anchor, or an eval ref pointing at a missing artifact each exit the gate red.
CLM-0008 [verified]: A claim marked verified without at least one test evidence ref fails claims:check.
CLM-0009 [verified]: Every audit event is hash-chained: a chain of appended events verifies end-to-end with its exact length.
CLM-0010 [verified]: Every audit envelope carries the contracts surface version it was written under.
CLM-0011 [verified]: A single bit flipped anywhere in a stored audit record is detected and attributed to its sequence number.
CLM-0012 [verified]: Truncating, reordering, or deleting audit log entries fails verification.
CLM-0013 [verified]: Tamper evidence is property-tested: across seeded random chains, every single-byte mutation of the audit log file fails verification.
CLM-0014 [verified]: The event bus delivers only the five frozen contracts: publishing a malformed or unknown message type is rejected at the boundary.
CLM-0015 [verified]: The manifest registry rejects invalid manifests at registration and is the single source of capability truth for lookup.
CLM-0016 [verified]: The ladder blocks any routed action whose required tier exceeds the manifest's tier or the task's authorityCeiling.
CLM-0017 [verified]: Every tier transition (promotion, demotion) is recorded to the audit chain; demotion on threshold breach is automatic.
CLM-0018 [verified]: The event bus applies backpressure when a subscriber's queue is full rather than dropping events silently.
CLM-0019 [verified]: Adapter subprocess calls capture stdout, stderr, and exit code, and enforce wall-clock timeouts.
CLM-0020 [verified]: Every adapter call is metered — tokens, usd, and duration — and reported in the contracts Cost shape.
CLM-0021 [verified]: Adapters expose one uniform interface across model CLIs; an unavailable CLI is reported as unavailable, never stubbed.
CLM-0022 [verified]: Semantic memory rejects writes without provenance.
CLM-0023 [verified]: Semantic recall ranks facts by provenance and recency, and unrefreshed facts decay below fresher ones.
CLM-0024 [verified]: Episodic memory persists each Outcome as a summary plus a pointer to the full trace, retrievable by task id.
CLM-0025 [verified]: Memory state is repo-local SQLite; deleting the database file leaves the system functional with empty memory.
CLM-0026 [verified]: The router matches a TaskContract to manifests by capability and budget, and returns the routing decision without executing when asked to plan only.
CLM-0027 [verified]: The router never routes to a manifest whose tier exceeds the task's authorityCeiling.
CLM-0028 [verified]: A floor of exploration traffic guarantees demoted-but-registered capabilities still receive routing consideration.
CLM-0029 [verified]: The context compiler is deterministic: identical inputs produce byte-identical Briefs under a pinned compiler version.
CLM-0030 [verified]: Brief sections respect hard token budgets with priority-ordered drop, and every section carries provenance.
CLM-0031 [verified]: The quality gate runs typecheck, lint, test, and coverage over a workspace and emits a structured Verdict with severity-tagged findings.
CLM-0032 [verified]: Every quality-gate Verdict appends to the audit chain.
CLM-0033 [verified]: The MCP surface exposes exactly the kernel eleven — run, status, brief, gate, recall, remember, distill, forge, manifest, audit, observe — and nothing else.
CLM-0034 [verified]: The run entry point routes a TaskContract via manifests and returns an Outcome, with every routing decision audited.
CLM-0035 [verified]: The audit tool queries events and verifies the chain on demand.
CLM-0036 [verified]: One real task runs end-to-end through the quality gate, producing a Verdict, an Outcome, and a verifiable audit chain.
CLM-0037 [verified]: The vote gate aggregates a panel of voters into one Verdict under simple-majority, super-majority, or unanimous strategies — three voters by default, seven at plan ratification.
CLM-0038 [verified]: Every voter's vote and reasoning is recorded as a VoterRecord, feeding the per-voter precision series.
CLM-0039 [verified]: Voters on one gate panel share a single compiled Brief — one compile, n voters.
CLM-0040 [verified]: Workforce agents are configuration, not generation: PM, Coder, Reviewer, Documenter, and Researcher templates instantiate as manifests, and new templates enter at suggest tier.
CLM-0041 [verified]: The PM decomposes a ratified plan into child TaskContracts whose budgets must sum within the parent's budget.
CLM-0042 [verified]: The canonical loop is declared as data: every edge carries a contract and every gate node emits a Verdict.
CLM-0043 [verified]: The vote-iterate cycle is bounded at K iterations (default 3) before escalating to the human.
CLM-0044 [verified]: Per-node checkpoints make any run resumable: a run killed mid-loop resumes from its last checkpoint and completes.
CLM-0045 [verified]: A repo overlay overrides gate thresholds, K, budgets, and loop nodes as data — never by duplicating the graph.
CLM-0046 [verified]: The full canonical loop has run on a real feature in a real repository, end to end through vote and quality gates.
CLM-0047 [verified]: The review gate performs adversarial diff review at advisory tier, and every voter's precision is recorded into the fitness ledger.
CLM-0048 [verified]: Review-gate calibration is measured against the labeled n=10 eval set ported from v1.
CLM-0049 [verified]: Distill proposes a SKILL.md from an episodic trace, entering the ladder at suggest tier.
CLM-0050 [verified]: Skills enter the procedural library only through the distill ratification path.
CLM-0051 [verified]: Forge refuses to build a workshop tool unless its spec carries a claim entry, an acceptance test, and a manifest first.
CLM-0052 [verified]: Workshop tools are generated and tested only inside the sandbox profile — no network by default, filesystem scoped to a scratch directory.
CLM-0053 [verified]: Workshop tools live under the workshop namespace, cannot import kernel or faculty internals, and are capped at twelve per overlay — at cap, forging requires retiring.
CLM-0054 [verified]: Workshop tools are born at suggest, reach advisory only after N clean audited runs, reach enforce only with human ratification, and decay toward removal when unused.
CLM-0055 [verified]: The Observer maintains the fitness ledger — invocations, success correlation, cost, recency — and the per-voter precision series.
CLM-0056 [verified]: The Observer files issues about the system itself at suggest tier, and self-filed issues re-enter the canonical loop with no privileged path.
CLM-0057 [planned]: A distilled skill and a forged workshop tool have both been born through gates.
CLM-0058 [verified]: Distill and forge complete the MCP surface at exactly the kernel eleven.

sections.content:
CLM-0001 [verified]: Kernloop's five contracts are zod-validated: malformed messages — missing fields, unknown enum values, wrong types, negative budgets — are rejected at parse time.
CLM-0002 [verified]: The authority ladder is a closed four-tier enum — observe, suggest, advisory, enforce — and any other tier value is rejected at parse time.
CLM-0003 [verified]: All five contracts survive JSON round-trip serialization: parsing the stringified form of a valid contract yields a value equal to the original.
CLM-0004 [verified]: The contract surface is frozen at exactly five types — TaskContract, Brief, Verdict, Outcome, Manifest — and references to any contract outside the five are rejected.
CLM-0005 [verified]: Manifests carry governance as data: authority tier, maturity, optional promotion threshold, and claim references are schema-enforced, with unknown tiers and malformed claim ids rejected at parse time.
CLM-0006 [verified]: All five contracts reject unknown top-level keys, so field drift fails at parse time instead of passing silently across the bus.
CLM-0007 [verified]: claims:check fails on dangling evidence — a test ref naming a nonexistent test, a CI ref naming a nonexistent job, a doc ref with a missing anchor, or an eval ref pointing at a missing artifact each exit the gate red.
CLM-0008 [verified]: A claim marked verified without at least one test evidence ref fails claims:check.
CLM-0009 [verified]: Every audit event is hash-chained: a chain of appended events verifies end-to-end with its exact length.
CLM-0010 [verified]: Every audit envelope carries the contracts surface version it was written under.
CLM-0011 [verified]: A single bit flipped anywhere in a stored audit record is detected and attributed to its sequence number.
CLM-0012 [verified]: Truncating, reordering, or deleting audit log entries fails verification.
CLM-0013 [verified]: Tamper evidence is property-tested: across seeded random chains, every single-byte mutation of the audit log file fails verification.
CLM-0014 [verified]: The event bus delivers only the five frozen contracts: publishing a malformed or unknown message type is rejected at the boundary.
CLM-0015 [verified]: The manifest registry rejects invalid manifests at registration and is the single source of capability truth for lookup.
CLM-0016 [verified]: The ladder blocks any routed action whose required tier exceeds the manifest's tier or the task's authorityCeiling.
CLM-0017 [verified]: Every tier transition (promotion, demotion) is recorded to the audit chain; demotion on threshold breach is automatic.
CLM-0018 [verified]: The event bus applies backpressure when a subscriber's queue is full rather than dropping events silently.
CLM-0019 [verified]: Adapter subprocess calls capture stdout, stderr, and exit code, and enforce wall-clock timeouts.
CLM-0020 [verified]: Every adapter call is metered — tokens, usd, and duration — and reported in the contracts Cost shape.
CLM-0021 [verified]: Adapters expose one uniform interface across model CLIs; an unavailable CLI is reported as unavailable, never stubbed.
CLM-0022 [verified]: Semantic memory rejects writes without provenance.
CLM-0023 [verified]: Semantic recall ranks facts by provenance and recency, and unrefreshed facts decay below fresher ones.
CLM-0024 [verified]: Episodic memory persists each Outcome as a summary plus a pointer to the full trace, retrievable by task id.
CLM-0025 [verified]: Memory state is repo-local SQLite; deleting the database file leaves the system functional with empty memory.
CLM-0026 [verified]: The router matches a TaskContract to manifests by capability and budget, and returns the routing decision without executing when asked to plan only.
CLM-0027 [verified]: The router never routes to a manifest whose tier exceeds the task's authorityCeiling.
CLM-0028 [verified]: A floor of exploration traffic guarantees demoted-but-registered capabilities still receive routing consideration.
CLM-0029 [verified]: The context compiler is deterministic: identical inputs produce byte-identical Briefs under a pinned compiler version.
CLM-0030 [verified]: Brief sections respect hard token budgets with priority-ordered drop, and every section carries provenance.
CLM-0031 [verified]: The quality gate runs typecheck, lint, test, and coverage over a workspace and emits a structured Verdict with severity-tagged findings.
CLM-0032 [verified]: Every quality-gate Verdict appends to the audit chain.
CLM-0033 [verified]: The MCP surface exposes exactly the kernel eleven — run, status, brief, gate, recall, remember, distill, forge, manifest, audit, observe — and nothing else.
CLM-0034 [verified]: The run entry point routes a TaskContract via manifests and returns an Outcome, with every routing decision audited.
CLM-0035 [verified]: The audit tool queries events and verifies the chain on demand.
CLM-0036 [verified]: One real task runs end-to-end through the quality gate, producing a Verdict, an Outcome, and a verifiable audit chain.
CLM-0037 [verified]: The vote gate aggregates a panel of voters into one Verdict under simple-majority, super-majority, or unanimous strategies — three voters by default, seven at plan ratification.
CLM-0038 [verified]: Every voter's vote and reasoning is recorded as a VoterRecord, feeding the per-voter precision series.
CLM-0039 [verified]: Voters on one gate panel share a single compiled Brief — one compile, n voters.
CLM-0040 [verified]: Workforce agents are configuration, not generation: PM, Coder, Reviewer, Documenter, and Researcher templates instantiate as manifests, and new templates enter at suggest tier.
CLM-0041 [verified]: The PM decomposes a ratified plan into child TaskContracts whose budgets must sum within the parent's budget.
CLM-0042 [verified]: The canonical loop is declared as data: every edge carries a contract and every gate node emits a Verdict.
CLM-0043 [verified]: The vote-iterate cycle is bounded at K iterations (default 3) before escalating to the human.
CLM-0044 [verified]: Per-node checkpoints make any run resumable: a run killed mid-loop resumes from its last checkpoint and completes.
CLM-0045 [verified]: A repo overlay overrides gate thresholds, K, budgets, and loop nodes as data — never by duplicating the graph.
CLM-0046 [verified]: The full canonical loop has run on a real feature in a real repository, end to end through vote and quality gates.
CLM-0047 [verified]: The review gate performs adversarial diff review at advisory tier, and every voter's precision is recorded into the fitness ledger.
CLM-0048 [verified]: Review-gate calibration is measured against the labeled n=10 eval set ported from v1.
CLM-0049 [verified]: Distill proposes a SKILL.md from an episodic trace, entering the ladder at suggest tier.
CLM-0050 [verified]: Skills enter the procedural library only through the distill ratification path.
CLM-0051 [verified]: Forge refuses to build a workshop tool unless its spec carries a claim entry, an acceptance test, and a manifest first.
CLM-0052 [verified]: Workshop tools are generated and tested only inside the sandbox profile — no network by default, filesystem scoped to a scratch directory.
CLM-0053 [verified]: Workshop tools live under the workshop namespace, cannot import kernel or faculty internals, and are capped at twelve per overlay — at cap, forging requires retiring.
CLM-0054 [verified]: Workshop tools are born at suggest, reach advisory only after N clean audited runs, reach enforce only with human ratification, and decay toward removal when unused.
CLM-0055 [verified]: The Observer maintains the fitness ledger — invocations, success correlation, cost, recency — and the per-voter precision series.
CLM-0056 [verified]: The Observer files issues about the system itself at suggest tier, and self-filed issues re-enter the canonical loop with no privileged path.
CLM-0057 [planned]: A distilled skill and a forged workshop tool have both been born through gates.
CLM-0058 [verified]: Distill and forge complete the MCP surface at exactly the kernel eleven.

sections.name: plan
sections.content:
The plan is grounded: `skills/README.md` is currently five lines and already gestures at the distill path, and `skills/proposed/run-quality-gate-via-kernel/` exists as a live example of a suggest-tier proposal. Here is the PM decomposition.

## Implementation plan — append "Ratification path (P3)" to skills/README.md

**Scope assessment.** This is a single-file documentation task with no code, no new claims, and no contract changes. Both capability statements it documents are already verified (CLM-0049, CLM-0050), so the work is purely descriptive and the honest decomposition is one child task. Splitting further would burn budget on coordination for a section of prose.

**Child 1 of 1 — Documenter: write the section.**

*Goal.* Append a `## Ratification path (P3)` section to `skills/README.md`, leaving the existing five lines untouched. The section must state, in this order: (1) `distill` proposes a `SKILL.md` from an episodic trace and writes it to `skills/proposed/<name>/`, entering the authority ladder at **suggest** tier `[CLM-0049]`; (2) a proposed skill goes live only when a human moves `skills/proposed/<name>/` to `skills/<name>/` through a reviewed PR — that merge **is** the ratification, and skills enter the procedural library through no other path `[CLM-0050]`. It may cite the live example `skills/proposed/run-quality-gate-via-kernel/` as the current state of the queue. Every capability sentence carries its claim tag per the charter; no sentence may claim behavior beyond what CLM-0049/0050 attest.

*Files owned.* `skills/README.md` only. Any discovery outside this file (e.g., stale wording elsewhere) is reported back, not acted on.

*Evidence requirements.* No new claim entries — both claims exist and are verified. Evidence at integration: a diff whose only touched file is `skills/README.md`; the two claim tags present and resolving under `claims:check`; `governance:check` green (charter/doc consistency); lint green (LOC limits irrelevant here but the gate still runs).

*Definition of done.* Section appended; existing intro text unmodified; both claim tags present; `pnpm lint`, `pnpm claims:check`, and `pnpm governance:check` all green; quality gate emits a passing Verdict that appends to the audit chain. Done is the Verdict, not the diff.

*Budget slice.* The child receives **70%** of the parent budget on every metered dimension — tokens, usd, wall-clock duration — with authorityCeiling **suggest** (documentation proposal; the merge authority stays human). The parent PM retains the remaining **30%** as reserve for gate re-runs across the bounded vote-iterate cycle (K ≤ 3 per CLM-0043) and for integration verification. Sums check trivially: 70% + 30% = 100% on each dimension, within the parent on all three.

**Integration.** PM verifies the single-file constraint on the returned diff, runs the full gate suite, and routes the Verdict back through the loop. If the gate fails twice on wording (claim-tag or governance findings), iterate within K; on K exhaustion, escalate to the human rather than loosening the gate.

One open ambiguity, resolved narrow: the existing README line "enter only through the `distill` ratification path" slightly predates the new section and could be folded into it, but the brief says append and modify only — so the child appends and leaves that line alone; the PM notes the minor redundancy in the session report.

voters.reasoning: Grounding verified directly against the repo: skills/README.md is exactly the five lines the plan describes, and skills/proposed/run-quality-gate-via-kernel/ exists as the cited live example. The decomposition is honest about scope — one Documenter child for a prose-only change is the right granularity; splitting further would be coordination overhead with no verification benefit. Architectural soundness: both documented behaviors are already verified claims (CLM-0049, CLM-0050), so the task creates no new capability surface and the section is descriptive, satisfying the charter's claims-first rule without needing new registry entries. Claim tags on every capability sentence match the [CLM-xxxx] convention enforced by governance:check. Testability and workflow integration are strong: done is defined as gates green (lint, claims:check, governance:check) plus a quality-gate Verdict appended to the audit chain, all of which are existing automated pipelines — progress is verifiable at the single integration point, which is appropriate for a one-step task. Budget arithmetic is valid (70% child + 30% PM reserve on all metered dimensions, per CLM-0041's sum constraint), and authorityCeiling=suggest correctly keeps merge authority human per the ratification model being documented. The one ambiguity — the existing 'enter only through the distill ratification path' line slightly overlapping the new section — is resolved narrow (append only, report redundancy), exactly as the charter's 'when uncertain' clause directs. Minor residual redundancy in the README is an acceptable cost of respecting the modify-only-by-appending brief. No YAGNI, scope creep, or over-engineering concerns.

Security assessment: low-risk, documentation-only change. I verified the ground truth — skills/README.md is the five-line file described, and skills/proposed/run-quality-gate-via-kernel/ exists as the cited live example, so the proposal is not claiming unwired behavior. Both capability statements it documents (CLM-0049, CLM-0050) are already verified with resolving evidence. From a security standpoint the proposal is actually positive: documenting that suggest-tier proposals cannot self-promote and that ratification requires a human-reviewed PR merge hardens the human-in-the-loop privilege boundary against future erosion, and the plan correctly sets authorityCeiling=suggest on the child so no automated path gains merge authority. No injection surface, no secrets, no path traversal (the single-file constraint is verified on the returned diff at integration), no new dependencies, no resource-exhaustion vector — the 70/30 budget split with K≤3 bounded iteration caps spend. Workflow-test assessment: fully testable and incrementally verifiable — the diff constraint is mechanically checkable, claim-tag presence resolves under claims:check, governance:check enforces charter/doc consistency, and done is defined as a passing audited Verdict rather than the diff itself, fitting the existing CI pipeline exactly. The narrow resolution of the pre-existing redundant README line (report, don't touch) respects scope discipline. One minor note, not blocking: escalation on K exhaustion rather than gate-loosening is the correct fail-closed posture. No SECURITY_RISK, YAGNI, or SCOPE_CREEP concerns apply.

Existing-tool check: not applicable in the usual sense — this is project-specific documentation of kernloop's own ratification mechanism; no external tool (no off-the-shelf doc generator, no README template) can describe this repo's distill→proposed→ratified flow, so the buy column is empty by construction. Kill-the-feature option: evaluated and worse — CLM-0049/0050 are verified behavior, skills/proposed/run-quality-gate-via-kernel/ already sits in the queue, and an undocumented ratification path invites the exact failure this repo guards against (an agent or human moving a skill live without the reviewed-PR ratification, or claiming the path works without it being written down where contributors look). The charter requires docs updated with capability statements tagged [CLM-xxxx]; leaving the README silent on a live, gated mechanism is the drift, not the addition. Mission alignment: direct — documenting the authority-ladder ratification path is core to the governed-faculties thesis, not sprawl. Sprawl audit: the README already gestures at the distill path; this extends the same file rather than forking a new doc, and the plan explicitly resolves the minor redundancy with the existing line narrowly (append-only, report the overlap) rather than expanding scope. Scope discipline is exemplary: one file owned, one child task (correctly refusing to over-decompose prose), no new claims minted, budget sums checked, authorityCeiling held at suggest. Workflow-test assessment: verifiable via existing gates — claims:check confirms both tags resolve, governance:check confirms charter/doc consistency, lint runs, and done is defined as a passing Verdict appended to the audit chain, so the change is testable and incrementally verifiable within the existing CI pipeline. No YAGNI (the mechanism already exists and is in use), no OVER_ENGINEERING (single documenter child), no SCOPE_CREEP (explicit single-file constraint with discovery-report-only rule). Approve.
